approach: Route by the presence of the five-field brief, in code. In `decide()` (steward.rs) a change with a brief is owner-bound: it is never applied, whatever the rung, and is recorded as `Decision::Proposed` with the brief and kind Proposal. A change without a brief is applied if `role.may_change(rung)`; otherwise it is recorded with brief None and does not reach the owner. In work_decisions.rs `open_proposals` lists an undecided proposal only if it has a brief, or has none and the raising role may change its rung (the drain approves those, and the audience role's items rely on that). `in_limit` returns false for a briefed item, so the drain never auto-approves an owner-bound item. A new constructor gives a blind spot that needs a token or environment change a brief, and `validate_items` passes the model's checked brief to it; a briefed item no longer needs a request. `STEWARD_PROMPT` is rewritten to tell the steward to step back across repeated failures and blind spots, to decide and queue a request itself, and to write a brief only for an environment change or a token or credential. The prompt is kept inside the 600-token budget and the role goes to version 3. Tests cover each routing case in core and end to end in cli. A new context test composes the real prompt. The docs, CHANGELOG and a new decision entry are updated and mark the prompt rule prose-only and the routing code-enforced.

decisions.choice: Brief present means owner-bound, at any rung. `decide()` skips the apply step, returns `Decision::Proposed`, keeps the brief, and sets the work item kind to Proposal.
decisions.reason: Rejected-job finding 1: an env/token need at a rung the steward may change (a missing GH_TOKEN is an `implementation` blind spot) was applied and the owner never saw it. Setting kind Proposal is needed because `open_proposals` and `find_open` (work_decisions.rs:43, 93) only handle kind Proposal, so a briefed repeated-failure or blind-spot item would otherwise stay invisible.

rejected.option: Keep applying in-limit changes and attach the brief only above the limit (the base behavior, steward.rs:709).
rejected.why: This is the fault: env/token needs never reach the owner, and above-limit changes without a brief did.

rejected.option: Add a code check that refuses briefs for anything but env/token needs.
rejected.why: Out of scope. The prompt limits briefs (prose-only); code routes by brief presence.

decisions.choice: `open_proposals` lists an undecided proposal when `brief.is_some() || in_limit(records, item)`. `in_limit` gains `brief.is_none() &&`. `split_open` is unchanged and so sends briefed items to 'above' (a person) and unbriefed in-limit items to 'within' (drain).
decisions.reason: Finding 2: unbriefed above-limit proposals must not be listed. The assumption text says 'only items with a brief', but the audience role raises unbriefed Implementation proposals that its own cli test expects in `status.work_proposals` (crates/athena-cli/tests/audience.rs:149). That role records its definition in the same commit (audience.rs:333), so they are in limit, and the drain approves them. Keeping in-limit unbriefed items listed leaves that role and the drain unchanged. Criteria 1 and 2 hold.

rejected.option: List only items with a brief.
rejected.why: It hides the audience role's work items from `athena status` and breaks the audience tests, and the audience role is out of scope.
Not needed. `split_open` already partitions `open_proposals` by `in_limit`, and the new `in_limit` gives the right split.

decisions.choice: A briefed blind spot gets a new constructor `blind_spot_needing_owner(source, title, brief)`. `validate_items` calls it for a blind-spot item that carries a brief, after `check_brief`. A blind spot without a brief still goes through `blind_spot_change`.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3. The output schema already has an optional `brief` on every item (crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs:322), so no schema change is needed. Only the model can tell a missing token from a transient gh error, so the model decides whether to write a brief, and the prompt (prose-only) limits it to env/token needs.

rejected.option: Make the blind-spot constructor detect GH_TOKEN itself.
rejected.why: The steward's own process cannot see the model's gh environment; the token passing lives in athena-agent env.rs, outside this change.
It changes outputs.rs, which is not a deliverable, and the schema, for no gain.

decisions.choice: `validate_items` requires a request for a rung the role may change only when the item has no brief.
decisions.reason: A briefed item is never applied, so a request would be dead text. Without this, an env/token item at `implementation` with no request is dropped at steward.rs:961 before it reaches `decide()`.

rejected.option: Keep requiring a request for every in-limit item.
rejected.why: It forces dead text, or drops the owner-bound item.

decisions.choice: Keep two `Decision` variants. `Proposed` doc: 'not applied; the work item is recorded'. Whether the owner sees it depends on the item's brief.
decisions.reason: A third variant would touch `run()` and every match for no behavior gain; the item's brief is the measured signal the criteria name.

rejected.why: More churn in `run()` and tests; the owner-visible fact is the brief, not the variant.

decisions.choice: The prompt fits by rewriting `STEWARD_PROMPT` in fewer bytes. The role goes to version 3. The ceiling is the composed contract (929 bytes, docs/decisions.md D168) plus the prompt: at most 1800 bytes (600 tokens × 3), so about 868 bytes of prompt.
decisions.reason: Budgets never rise to fit a set (lib.rs:176-178). The current prompt leaves about 150 bytes of room, so the producer must measure the real composed size. Criterion 5's test does that.

rejected.why: Forbidden by the budget comment; the criterion asserts at most 600.
